turns.text: quick q. need subnetting practice for the boss fight. it's my weak spot along with port numbers. been pulling questions from my practice test app but i keep seeing the same ones. can you give me different ones, hard ones pls

Happy to. Fresh, harder subnetting problems it is. Quick calibration so I don't waste your time: how comfortable are you with converting a CIDR prefix to a subnet mask and counting usable hosts? And how are your practice scores looking overall?
cidr to mask is ok, i just choke when it gets to splitting networks. averaging low 70s on practice exams, pass line is like 75 so i'm right under it. ugh

That's a fixable gap, since you're only a few points under. Splitting networks is mostly one repeated move. Here are 6 problems, no answers until you ask.

1. Given 192.168.10.0/24, you need at least 6 subnets. What new prefix do you use, and how many usable hosts per subnet?
2. What are the network address, broadcast address, and usable range for 172.16.45.130/26?
3. You have 10.0.0.0/22. List the first four /24 subnets inside it.
4. A department needs 58 hosts. What's the smallest prefix that works? What's the next smaller prefix that would fail, and why?
5. Is 192.168.5.200/27 in the same subnet as 192.168.5.225/27? Show your work.
6. Split 203.0.113.0/24 into subnets of 60, 28, and 12 hosts using VLSM. Give the network address and prefix for each.

Tip for splitting: find the block size (256 minus the interesting octet of the mask), then list the multiples of it. Everything falls out of that. Want port number drills mixed in too?
ok 1 is /27, 30 hosts. 3 is 10.0.0.0, 10.0.1.0, 10.0.2.0, 10.0.3.0. idk the rest yet. and yes mix in ports, those are nerfed for me

Both correct. Number 1 is /27 with 30 usable hosts, and number 3 is exactly right since a /22 holds four /24s.

On the rest, try block size for #2: a /26 mask's last octet is 192, so the block is 64. Which multiple of 64 sits just below 130?

Port drills, 8 rapid ones. Name the protocol and default port:
1. Secure remote shell
2. DNS
3. HTTPS
4. DHCP server
5. SMTP
6. RDP
7. Telnet
8. SNMP

Send what you've got on #2 and the ports, and I'll check them and give you 6 new subnetting problems.
2: 128 is the network so .128, broadcast .191, usable .129-.190. ports: ssh 22, dns 53, https 443, dhcp 67, smtp 25, rdp 3389, telnet 23, snmp 161. gg?

gg, that's all correct. Subnet #2 is right (network .128, broadcast .191, usable .129 to .190), and all 8 ports are right. DHCP server listens on 67, and clients use 68, which is a common trick question.

The pattern: when you find the block size first, you don't choke. Do #4 to #6 the same way and send them over. Then I'll make you a harder set mixing VLSM with a few port questions on the trickier ones (TFTP, LDAP, syslog, NTP).
